alphabetNote: Stoicheion presents 24 letter cards. The numeral table also includes the ancient signs digamma or stigma (6), koppa (90) and sampi (900).
layers: One deity has different numerical contexts
layersText: A deity has a name total, a digital root or pythmen, and numbers that appear in myths. Letters give the name total. The pythmen opens its sacred meaning. Numbers in a myth reveal the situation in which a power acts.
thirteenText: The circle of thirteen deities of the Aurora Order includes Hestia, the keeper of the hearth, and Dionysus, the power of transformation. Together they reveal a stable support for life and the ability to renew itself.
sectorMapNote: Each sphere of Theokyklos reveals a certain side of life through its divine patrons. Below are the names, their letter calculations and the pythmen of the total amount.
restorationText: In numerical restoration, the original reading gives the root we seek to recover. Add the card, resource and support-word values. Check their digital root, then choose the resource whose meaning helps with the situation.
restorationExample: For example, an original total of 20 gives root 2, the dyad: a relationship between two sides. Card Α(1), resource Η(8) and the support word ΕΔΡΑ = 110 give 1 + 8 + 110 = 119 → 11 → 2. Resource Π(80) also restores the dyad: 1 + 80 + 110 = 191 → 11 → 2. Choose the letter through its meaning in Stoicheion.
restorationNote: ΕΣΤΙΑ is Hestia’s name; ΕΔΡΑ means a seat or foundation. In restoration, ΕΔΡΑ expresses the stability created by a hearth.
sourceNote: Open the source to read the entire myth or argument. The cards contain their main images and numerical connections.
methodText: Myth reveals the gods’ relationships and the meaning of events. Letter calculations make numerical connections visible. The sages of the Aurora Order bring these paths together to illuminate their meaning in human life.
normalization: Each Greek letter has its own value. Accents and breathing marks preserve that value; ς and Σ both equal 200. Choose another form of a name to see its letters produce a different total.
kronosText: ΚΡΟΝΟΣ - Kronos, father of Zeus; ΧΡΟΝΟΣ — Chronos, time. ΚΡΟΝΟΣ = 510; ΧΡΟΝΟΣ = 1090. Kappa Κ(20) and chi Χ(600) reveal different numerical paths of these images.

deity.zeus.ancient: In Plato’s Cratylus, Zeus’s name is read through the idea of the one through whom living beings have life. In the Iliad, Zeus, Poseidon and Hades divide the sky, sea and underworld; earth and Olympus remain shared.
deity.zeus.sacred: The triad expresses the world divided among three brothers. The name’s root is 9, the ennead: a completed order in which every power has its place.
deity.zeus.formula: ΖΕΥΣ = 612 = 36 × 17, with 36 = 6 × 6. Picture six rows of six places: a clear image of proportion and arrangement. The sages of the Aurora Order use it to reveal Zeus’s power to gather many parts into one order.
deity.zeus.meaning: Zeus appears in decisions for which we are willing to answer. His power helps establish a fair rule, see the whole and bring personal will into accord with the common good.
deity.zeus.bridge: Zenith is the sphere of Zeus and Hera. Authority gains stability through union and promises kept. Hestia’s hearth offers the next step: give the decision a place in everyday life.
deity.zeus.limits: The name ΖΕΥΣ reveals the order of the whole. The form ΔΙΟΣ and the word ΘΕΟΣ occur in the number 284: the divine principle and the life-giving power of Zeus receive a common numerical image.
deity.zeus.word.0.note: The word "god" and the form of the name ΔΙΟΣ have the same sum of 284. In the Aurora Order’s interpretation, this is the connection of the divine principle with the power of Zeus.
deity.zeus.word.1.note: Life reveals the image of Zeus as the source of life, which Socrates discusses in Cratylus.
deity.zeus.word.2.note: The law turns a personal decision into a rule that is understandable to both the ruler himself and other people.
deity.zeus.word.3.note: Order means that every part has its place. This is the reference word of the zenith sphere.
deity.zeus.situation.0.title: Decisions and responsibility
deity.zeus.situation.0.body: Choose a rule that you are ready to follow yourself. The power of Zeus becomes a pillar when responsibility matches authority.
deity.zeus.situation.1.title: Union and management
deity.zeus.situation.1.body: Agree on roles and promises. Hera helps make the decision sustainable: everyone understands their contribution and can rely on the other.
deity.zeus.situation.2.title: A dispute over boundaries
deity.zeus.situation.2.body: Remember the three allotted realms: a shared undertaking grows stronger when each side has a recognised area of independence.
deity.hera.ancient: In the Cratylus, Hera’s name is linked with air. The Homeric hymn praises her as queen of the immortals and wife of Zeus. Air and union meet in the image of a space that sustains life.
deity.hera.sacred: The pentad, 5, expresses marriage: 2 + 3 = 5 joins even and odd principles. Hera’s name has root 1, the monad: unity around which a shared household is built.
deity.hera.formula: ΗΡΑ = 109; ΑΗΡ = 109. Hera’s name and the word for air contain the same letters in a different order. Their equal totals reveal one composition opening into two related images.
deity.hera.meaning: Hera reveals the strength of a mutual promise. As air gives room to breathe, a faithful union offers confidence and space to live. The sages of the Aurora Order add a numerical demonstration in the Pythagorean style to Plato’s connection between the words.
deity.hera.bridge: Zenith is the sphere of Zeus and Hera. Zeus establishes a shared order; Hera makes it a living union. Hestia adds the warmth of home and daily care.
deity.hera.limits: Hera helps to connect the dignity of everyone with the unity of the union. Reciprocity grows where promises are clear and loyalty is demonstrated in actions.
deity.hera.word.0.note: The same letters and total as Hera’s name: air sustains life, and a faithful union sustains a shared world.
deity.hera.word.1.note: Marriage reveals freely accepted commitments and a shared future.
deity.hera.word.2.note: Loyalty is a promise that is confirmed by deeds.
deity.hera.word.3.note: Harmony connects different voices so that each remains audible.
deity.hera.situation.0.title: Relationships
deity.hera.situation.0.body: Name one mutual promise and specify what it means for each.
deity.hera.situation.1.title: Shared work
deity.hera.situation.1.body: Agree on rules that protect the dignity of both parties.
deity.hera.situation.2.title: Lack of space
deity.hera.situation.2.body: Artemis's personal boundaries help Hera's union remain free and alive.
deity.poseidon.ancient: In the Iliad, Poseidon receives the sea when the three brothers divide the world. The hymns call him earth-shaker, tamer of horses and saviour of ships. His image joins depth, movement and immense power.
deity.poseidon.sacred: The triad appears in the world’s three allotted realms and in the trident, Poseidon’s sign of authority. His name has root 4, the tetrad: power finding a channel and steady banks.
deity.poseidon.formula: ΠΟΣΕΙΔΩΝ = 1219 = 23 × 53. Root 4 expresses stability amid movement. The epic form ΠΟΣΕΙΔΑΩΝ = 1220 adds Α(1), reaching root 5, the pentad: a union of different principles.
deity.poseidon.meaning: Poseidon reveals the depth of feeling and the force of inner movement. In the Aurora Order’s interpretation, the sea becomes an image of the soul’s life: we learn to hear its currents and keep our course.
deity.poseidon.bridge: West is the sphere of Poseidon and Amphitrite. Together they reveal the sea as power and a living realm. Nadir continues the theme of depth; Apollo’s clarity helps us keep a bearing among the waves.
deity.poseidon.limits: The waters of the psyche are an image of the deep life of the soul in the Aurora Order’s interpretation. A feeling gets its shores when we name it, understand the reason and choose a meaningful action.
deity.poseidon.word.0.note: The sea contains current, storm and silence - different states of one element.
deity.poseidon.word.1.note: Flow reveals the continuous movement of feelings and events.
deity.poseidon.word.2.note: Sea calm helps to understand inner peace: strength is preserved, movement becomes smooth.
deity.poseidon.word.3.note: Depth connects the sea with the search for hidden support; in Theokyklos it is also the word nadir.
deity.poseidon.situation.0.title: Strong feeling
deity.poseidon.situation.0.body: Name the feeling and the event that caused it. Then choose an action that preserves your shores.
deity.poseidon.situation.1.title: Lost direction
deity.poseidon.situation.1.body: Refer to Apollo's clarity: identify one reference point against which you can check your course.
deity.poseidon.situation.2.title: Support and hidden resources
deity.poseidon.situation.2.body: Ask yourself what you can rely on under the surface of events: experience, a loyal person, a skill or a reserve of time.
deity.demeter.ancient: In the hymn, Demeter searches for Persephone for nine days and receives news at the tenth dawn. A yearly cycle is established: her daughter spends one third below and two thirds with her mother and the gods.
deity.demeter.sacred: In the Aurora Order’s interpretation, root 9 connects Demeter’s name with her nine-day search for Persephone. Nine is the ennead, completion: the search draws to an end and opens a path to return. Ten, the decad, expresses a new complete cycle.
deity.demeter.formula: ΔΗΜΗΤΗΡ = 468 = 36 × 13. Zeus’s name gives 612 = 36 × 17. The shared factor 36 connects two images of order: Zeus’s sky and Demeter’s fertile earth. The ratio 468:612 = 13:17 shows their distinct proportions.
deity.demeter.meaning: Demeter reveals the care that allows life to ripen. Her power appears in nourishment, patience and the ability to restore a connection with what we cherish.
deity.demeter.bridge: Southwest is Demeter’s sphere: nourishment, growth and harvest. Hades and Persephone’s nadir connects her to the hidden part of the yearly cycle. Persephone’s return brings hidden ripening into visible bloom.
deity.demeter.limits: Nine days of searching, the tenth dawn and the return of Persephone help to see the rhythm: to search, find support and let life grow again.
deity.demeter.word.0.note: The earth accepts the seed and gives it room to grow.
deity.demeter.word.1.note: Mother reveals the nourishing and protective power of Demeter.
deity.demeter.word.2.note: Grain connects the fertility of the earth with human labor and everyday food.
deity.demeter.word.3.note: Harvest is the visible result of time, care and ripening.
deity.demeter.situation.0.title: Exhaustion
deity.demeter.situation.0.body: Begin with simple care: eat, rest or put your living space in order. Support what you hope will bear fruit.
deity.demeter.situation.1.title: Waiting for a result
deity.demeter.situation.1.body: Divide the work into sowing, tending and harvesting. Identify the current stage and the care it needs.
deity.demeter.situation.2.title: Loss and return
deity.demeter.situation.2.body: The myth of Persephone gives an image of separation and return. Give the experience time and find what supports you today.
deity.athena.ancient: The Cratylus connects Athena with mind and divine understanding. The Theology of Arithmetic names seven after her: independent and maidenly, like the goddess born from Zeus’s head.
deity.athena.sacred: The heptad, 7, expresses the independence of intelligence. Within 1–10, seven has a special position: multiplying two integers greater than one never produces it, and doubling it takes us beyond the decad.
deity.athena.formula: ΑΘΗΝΑ = 69; ΑΚΜΗ = 69. Akme means a summit or prime of life: skill reaching maturity. Root 6, the hexad, expresses coordinated parts. A clear design meets precise execution.
deity.athena.meaning: Athena helps us recognise what matters, form a plan and choose a precise action. Her wisdom appears where knowledge becomes skill and readiness becomes timely action.
deity.athena.bridge: North is Athena’s sphere: clear thought, strategy and skill. Hephaestus develops her design in material. Α, Θ, Η, Ν form the name; Ζ(7) opens the numerical image of the heptad.
deity.athena.limits: Six reveals the consistency of the name, seven - the independence of wisdom. In the Aurora Order’s interpretation, these numbers help to see Athena as both the creator of order and the free mind.
deity.athena.word.0.note: The summit and maturity of skill: this word has the same total, 69, as Athena’s name.
deity.athena.word.1.note: The mind distinguishes the main thing and connects observations into an understandable picture.
deity.athena.word.2.note: Wisdom combines knowledge with the ability to choose the appropriate action.
deity.athena.word.3.note: Metis - reasonable resourcefulness; in the myth, Metis is also the mother of Athena.
deity.athena.situation.0.title: Difficult choice
deity.athena.situation.0.body: Write down separately what you know, what you suspect, and what you can do.
deity.athena.situation.1.title: Readiness to act
deity.athena.situation.1.body: Assess readiness by one clear sign: what skill or condition already allows you to act?
deity.athena.situation.2.title: Thought without embodiment
deity.athena.situation.2.body: Choose the first step of Hephaestus: make a sketch, assemble a sample, or test the idea in the work.
deity.apollo.ancient: Hesiod connects the seventh day with Apollo’s birth. Plutarch explores the Delphic letter Ε through the number five and reflects on the god’s unity. Apollo’s music gathers separate sounds into a harmonious whole.
deity.apollo.sacred: The monad, 1, expresses unity; the pentad, 5, is the living centre of the Delphic Ε; the heptad, 7, marks the sacred day of birth. The name has root 8, the ogdoad: developed form and consonance.
deity.apollo.formula: A musical fifth has ratio 3:2; a fourth has ratio 4:3. Together they make an octave: (3/2) × (4/3) = 2. For 6 and 12, the arithmetic mean is 9: 9 − 6 = 12 − 9 = 3. The harmonic mean is 8: 8/6 = 4/3 and 12/8 = 3/2.
deity.apollo.meaning: Apollo reveals clarity, measure and a well-ordered rhythm. His power helps us set aside excess, hear a fitting proportion and give experience a clear form.
deity.apollo.bridge: Northwest is Apollo’s sphere. Artemis’s northeast complements clarity with care for living integrity. Both main names have root 8, the ogdoad: fullness of form and agreement of levels.
deity.apollo.limits: The musical measure of Apollo teaches how to coordinate parts. Clarity becomes alive when there is room in it for the movement of Dionysus and the independence of Artemis.
deity.apollo.variant.2: Paian: name and type of song
deity.apollo.word.0.note: Measure helps to choose what is sufficient and determine the boundary.
deity.apollo.word.1.note: The lyre transforms individual strings into a coordinated tuning.
deity.apollo.word.2.note: Light makes differences visible and helps you find direction.
deity.apollo.word.3.note: The Soothsayer reveals Apollo's connection to the oracle and the search for the meaning of signs.
deity.apollo.situation.0.title: Noise and overload
deity.apollo.situation.0.body: Choose one main idea and one way to test it. Give your attention a clear direction.
deity.apollo.situation.1.title: Disturbed rhythm
deity.apollo.situation.1.body: Restore rhythm through a simple sequence: work, pause, end. The musical measure serves as an image of such coordination.
deity.apollo.situation.2.title: When clarity becomes rigid
deity.apollo.situation.2.body: Add the freedom of Dionysus: try a new way of expression while maintaining one clear reference point.
deity.artemis.ancient: The Cratylus links Artemis’s name with being whole and unharmed. In the hymns she hunts, leads dances and keeps her independence. With Athena and Hestia, she belongs to the three goddesses free from Aphrodite’s sway.
deity.artemis.sacred: Athena, Artemis and Hestia form a triad of independence: mind, personal boundaries and hearth. Artemis’s name has root 8, the ogdoad: the integrity of a living form.
deity.artemis.formula: ΑΡΤΕΜΙΣ = 656 = 16 × 41. ΑΡΤΕΜΗΣ = 654 means whole or unharmed. Ι(10) and Η(8) produce the difference of 2. The similar sound connects the name to preserved integrity.
deity.artemis.meaning: Artemis protects our living space: body, time, independence and what is still growing. Her power helps us preserve a boundary and remain open to the world.
deity.artemis.bridge: Northeast is Artemis’s sphere. Mythic kinship and root 8, the ogdoad, connect her with Apollo. Clarity and integrity support each other.
deity.artemis.limits: Artemis's integrity begins with respect for her space. A secure boundary allows for growth, choice, and voluntary connection.
deity.artemis.word.0.note: Intact means preserved integrity; this word reveals the name in Plato's reasoning.
deity.artemis.word.1.note: Sacred purity is an image of space that is preserved for what is important.
deity.artemis.word.2.note: Nature reveals the birth, growth and own rhythm of the living.
deity.artemis.word.3.note: The boundary helps to distinguish one’s space and the conditions under which a meeting is possible.
deity.artemis.situation.0.title: Protecting boundaries
deity.artemis.situation.0.body: State what you agree to and where the limit is. Keep it short and calm.
deity.artemis.situation.1.title: Tired of control
deity.artemis.situation.1.body: Leave room for voluntary communication. Hera helps negotiate, preserving Artemis's independence.
deity.artemis.situation.2.title: Return to nature
deity.artemis.situation.2.body: Take time to observe the living world: a tree, sky, water or changing light. Bring your attention back to the natural rhythm.
deity.ares.ancient: The hymn to Ares asks for courage, mastery of anger and a peaceful life. In the Iliad his fierce power meets Athena’s strategy; in the Odyssey his bond with Aphrodite joins passion to action.
deity.ares.sacred: Ares’s name has root 3, the triad: an impulse finds direction and becomes an action. In the Aurora Order’s interpretation, power moves through three steps: feel the impulse, choose a goal, act.
deity.ares.formula: ΑΡΗΣ = 309 = 3 × 103. Aphrodite’s name gives 993. Together, 309 + 993 = 1302 → 6: the hexad joins will and desire in a coordinated whole. Each name separately has root 3, the triad.
deity.ares.meaning: Ares gives us the resolve to begin, protect what matters and sustain an effort. Myth shows how reason, love and responsibility for consequences give that power direction.
deity.ares.bridge: South is the sphere of Ares and Aphrodite: action meets attraction. Athena helps choose a strategy; Aphrodite reveals the relationship for which power acts.
deity.ares.limits: The courage of Ares becomes a pillar when a person clearly understands what he is protecting. The peaceful life in the hymn is a worthy fruit of the power that one knows how to wield.
deity.ares.word.0.note: Impulse and anger reveal energy that requires direction.
deity.ares.word.1.note: Courage allows you to act in the face of difficulty and remain faithful to your chosen goal.
deity.ares.word.2.note: War reveals the ultimate clash of forces in the Ares mythos.
deity.ares.word.3.note: Peace is the fruit of mastered anger for which the hymn asks.
deity.ares.situation.0.title: A decisive step is needed
deity.ares.situation.0.body: Name one necessary step and the value for which you are taking it.
deity.ares.situation.1.title: Irritation
deity.ares.situation.1.body: First, give yourself a pause, then separate the fact from the reaction. Athena's clarity helps to choose the exact action.
deity.ares.situation.2.title: Will and desire
deity.ares.situation.2.body: Coordinate the desire and action with the other person. The southern couple reveals the power that knows how to hear the answer.
deity.aphrodite.ancient: In Hesiod, Aphrodite is born from sea foam. In Plato’s Symposium, Pausanias connects Urania and Pandemos with different aspects of love. Her image reveals attraction and the ability to create a bond.
deity.aphrodite.sacred: The pentad, 5, expresses union through 2 + 3 = 5. Aphrodite’s name has root 3, the triad: an encounter creates a new relationship and changes both lives.
deity.aphrodite.formula: ΑΦΡΟΔΙΤΗ = 993 = 3 × 331. ΟΥΡΑΝΙΑ = 632; ΠΑΝΔΗΜΟΣ = 453. Joined to the goddess’s name, these epithets give 1625 and 1446. An added aspect changes the numerical image: love unfolds through different relationships.
deity.aphrodite.meaning: Aphrodite helps us recognise another person’s value and the wish for connection. Her power appears in beauty, closeness, friendship and the new meaning an encounter creates.
deity.aphrodite.bridge: South is the sphere of Ares and Aphrodite. Attraction gains action; action gains a living purpose. The exit of Eros and Psyche continues the theme of love through which the soul comes to know itself.
deity.aphrodite.limits: Urania and Pandemos reveal different aspects of love in Pausanias’s speech. In the Aurora Order’s interpretation, each aspect helps us understand our feelings and the quality of a relationship.
deity.aphrodite.word.0.note: The foam recalls the sea birth of the goddess in Hesiod.
deity.aphrodite.word.1.note: Eros reveals the movement of attraction to what is loved.
deity.aphrodite.word.2.note: Friendship maintains a connection through trust, intimacy and shared experiences.
deity.aphrodite.word.3.note: Harmony helps different desires find coordinated expression.
deity.aphrodite.situation.0.title: Growing closer
deity.aphrodite.situation.0.body: Name what attracts you to another and see how reciprocity manifests itself.
deity.aphrodite.situation.1.title: Shared work
deity.aphrodite.situation.1.body: Discuss everyone's expectations and contributions. Hera helps turn attraction into a reliable promise.
deity.aphrodite.situation.2.title: Desire and action
deity.aphrodite.situation.2.body: Choose an action that expresses the feeling and respects the other person's response.
deity.hephaestus.ancient: In the hymn, Hephaestus and Athena teach people the arts. Hesiod names Aglaia, the radiant Grace, as his wife. In the Odyssey his story brings him together with Aphrodite and Ares: craft becomes a power that can restrain them.
deity.hephaestus.sacred: Hephaestus’s name has root 2, the dyad. In the Aurora Order’s interpretation, it is the meeting of design and material: a thing takes shape when its maker attends to what the material allows.
deity.hephaestus.formula: ΗΦΑΙΣΤΟΣ = 1289 is prime: its only positive divisors are 1 and itself. Its root is 2, the dyad. In craftsmanship this reveals two sides of the work: a clear design and the response of the material.
deity.hephaestus.meaning: Hephaestus turns an idea into a finished object. His power lies in patient repetition, precision, the ability to correct a mistake and the resolve to make something useful.
deity.hephaestus.bridge: Southeast is the sphere of Hephaestus and Aglaia: skill meets beautiful execution. Fire connects the forge to Hestia’s hearth: one shapes material, the other sustains the household.
deity.hephaestus.limits: Aglaia reveals the radiance of a well-made thing. Athena helps the plan, Hephaestus gives it form: thought and craft support each other.
deity.hephaestus.word.0.note: Craft is the ability to make a thing according to plan and test it in practice.
deity.hephaestus.word.1.note: The fire of the forge transforms material; the fire of the hearth sustains life.
deity.hephaestus.word.2.note: Work produces a result that someone can see, use or receive from its maker.
deity.hephaestus.word.3.note: Form makes the design tangible in the material.
deity.hephaestus.situation.0.title: A stalled project
deity.hephaestus.situation.0.body: Choose a small operation with a visible outcome: connect, check, repair or complete one part.
deity.hephaestus.situation.1.title: Beauty and quality
deity.hephaestus.situation.1.body: Look at the work through Aglaia’s eyes: is it convenient to use and is the quality of workmanship pleasing?
deity.hephaestus.situation.2.title: Idea without skill
deity.hephaestus.situation.2.body: First refine the idea with Athena, then test it on a small sample.
deity.hermes.ancient: The Cratylus connects Hermes with speech and interpretation. In the hymn he is born on the fourth day of the month and makes a seven-stringed lyre. Hymn XXIX joins Hermes and Hestia: the road meets the home.
deity.hermes.sacred: The tetrad, 4, appears in the day of Hermes’s birth; the heptad, 7, in the lyre’s seven strings. His name has root 2, the dyad: meaning travels between two sides and makes an encounter possible.
deity.hermes.formula: ΕΡΜΗΣ = 353; ΟΔΟΣ = 344. Their difference is 9, so both reach root 2, the dyad: Hermes connects people, a road connects places. ΛΟΓΟΣ = 373 expresses speech, another aspect of his power.
deity.hermes.meaning: Hermes helps us express a thought so another person can understand it, find a path between different positions and change our approach at the right moment.
deity.hermes.bridge: East is the sphere of Hermes and Peitho: clear speech meets persuasion. Hermes and Hephaestus share root 2, the dyad. One connects people through words; the other connects design to material.
deity.hermes.limits: The word of Hermes creates a meeting space. Persuasiveness increases when the meaning is clear, the arguments are clear, and the interlocutor can answer on his own.
deity.hermes.word.0.note: Logos connects the word, reasoning and a clear connection of thoughts.
deity.hermes.word.1.note: Interpretation helps to see the meaning and convey it to another.
deity.hermes.word.2.note: A road connects two places; pythmen 2, common with Hermes, reveals this connection.
deity.hermes.word.3.note: Peitho is the goddess of persuasion. Her name reveals the power of speech to resonate.
deity.hermes.situation.0.title: Important conversation
deity.hermes.situation.0.body: Say the main thing in one phrase and ask the interlocutor to convey how he understood it.
deity.hermes.situation.1.title: Disagreement
deity.hermes.situation.1.body: State the overall goal, then discuss the rationale and terms of agreement.
deity.hermes.situation.2.title: Road and return
deity.hermes.situation.2.body: Connect your journey with a place of return. Choose a place or activity that helps you gather your thoughts and regain your focus.
deity.hestia.ancient: The hymn gives Hestia the first and last libations. In Plato’s Phaedrus she keeps the gods’ home while the others follow their heavenly course. The Cratylus links her name with words for essence and being.
deity.hestia.sacred: The monad expresses the hearth as the beginning of shared space. First and last libations gather a rite into a whole. Hestia’s name has root 3, the triad: beginning, dwelling and return.
deity.hestia.formula: ΕΣΤΙΑ = 516 = 2² × 3 × 43. Root 3 expresses the triad of domestic rhythm. ΟΥΣΙΑ and ΕΣΣΙΑ are words for essence discussed by Plato: they illuminate the hearth as that around which life holds together.
deity.hestia.meaning: Hestia creates a place where we can gather ourselves and find support. Her power appears in care for the home, a steady rhythm and the simple acts that sustain life.
deity.hestia.bridge: The hearth is Hestia’s sphere, the inner ring of support. The centre is the sphere of Dionysus and Ariadne, where experience finds new meaning. Hestia gives transformation a place to begin and return to.
deity.hestia.limits: The hearth ring gathers life around a stable support. The word ΕΔΡΑ - "foundation, place" - reveals this power in the numerical restoration of the Aurora Order.
deity.hestia.word.0.note: Essence is what makes a thing exist and remain itself. Plato connects this question with the name of Hestia.

deity.hestia.word.2.note: A foundation gives something firm to rest on. This is the support word for the hearth in the Aurora Order’s numerical restoration.
deity.hestia.word.3.note: Home is a space that becomes inhabitable through constant care.

deity.hestia.situation.2.title: Completion

deity.dionysus.ancient: In the hymn, Dionysus transforms a ship: a vine and wondrous forms appear, and the sailors become dolphins. In Hesiod, Ariadne becomes his immortal wife. Plutarch brings Dionysus and Apollo together in the Delphic cycle.
deity.dionysus.sacred: In Plutarch’s Delphic account, three parts of the yearly cycle belong to Apollo and one to Dionysus. Dionysus’s name has root 5, the pentad: a living centre where different principles meet and give rise to something new.
deity.dionysus.formula: ΔΙΟΝΥΣΟΣ = 1004 = 4 × 251. ΑΡΙΑΔΝΗ = 174. Together, 1004 + 174 = 1178 → 17 → 8: the ogdoad expresses a fullness of experience to which Ariadne gives a coherent form.
deity.dionysus.meaning: Dionysus opens life to new expression. His power helps us move through intense experience, creativity and change; Ariadne keeps a thread of meaning through that movement.
deity.dionysus.bridge: The centre is the sphere of Dionysus and Ariadne. Different aspects of experience come together here. Their combined root 8, the ogdoad, connects them to the fullness of Apollo and Artemis; Hestia’s hearth gives the circle steady support.
deity.dionysus.limits: The transformation of Dionysus becomes fruitful when the experience gains meaning and expression. Ariadne's thread helps you take away from change what you can keep in life.
deity.dionysus.word.0.note: Wine in the myths of Dionysus reveals the festive transformation of ordinary life.
deity.dionysus.word.1.meaning: departure from an ordinary state; ecstasy
deity.dionysus.word.1.note: Ecstasis is a way out of a familiar position: an image of a strong experience that changes one’s perspective.
deity.dionysus.word.2.note: Ariadne connects transformation with the thread of meaning and, together with Dionysus, occupies the center of Theokyklos.
deity.dionysus.word.3.note: The word for life and Dionysus’s name both reach root 5: a meeting of different principles that opens new possibilities.
deity.dionysus.situation.0.title: Creative stagnation
deity.dionysus.situation.0.body: Try a different way to express the feeling: make a drawing, write a short text or find an image that captures it.
deity.dionysus.situation.1.title: Strong new impression
deity.dionysus.situation.1.body: Ask what thread of the new experience you want to preserve in a word, decision or deed.
deity.dionysus.situation.2.title: Excessive spontaneity
deity.dionysus.situation.2.body: Give the experience the form of Apollo and the place of Hestia: write down the main thing and return to one stable action.

number.1: Monad. Unity, beginning and focus. Gather your strength around one clear intention.
number.2: Dyad. Two principles in relationship: difference and mutuality. Hear both sides and find a way to connect them.
number.3: Triad. A whole developing through beginning, middle and completion. Intention becomes action and a result.
number.4: Tetrad. Stable form and order. Four supports give an undertaking a place, boundaries, sequence and reliability.
number.5: Pentad. Union and a living centre. The dyad and triad meet: 2 + 3 = 5 joins different principles.
number.6: Hexad. Proportion and the coordinated work of parts. 1 + 2 + 3 = 1 × 2 × 3 = 6: addition and multiplication reach the same whole.
number.7: Heptad. Independence and inner order. Seven holds a special place within the decad; ancient arithmology associates it with Athena.
number.8: Ogdoad. A fully developed form and the agreement of levels. 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 creates a three-dimensional cube; the musical octave returns to consonance.
number.9: Ennead. Completion and maturity. 3 × 3 = 9 unfolds the triad as a square and gathers the path travelled before a new beginning.
number.10: Decad: a complete numerical circle. The tetractys, 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10, brings beginning, relationship, development and stable form together.
arithmeticExtra: Tetractys is a triangle of four rows: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 points. Six and twenty-eight are called perfect numbers: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6; 1 + 2 + 4 + 7 + 14 = 28. Musical relationships show the coordination of parts: a 3:2 fifth and a 4:3 fourth together give an octave of 2:1.
mathematicalReading: This is a mathematical reading by the Aurora Order using the Pythagorean method.
nineWordsHint: Nine additional words, from monad to ennead
nineWordsIntro: Each word opens one aspect of divine power. Together, the nine roots form a complete circle. In the Aurora Order’s interpretation, the deities meet across all root numbers, revealing the breadth of their all-encompassing power.
mythMeeting: The myth and the relationship of powers
humanMeaning: How this appears in human life
pairRoot: The shared root of the combined names
sharedWord: A word for the shared context
rootKinship: The main names share a digital root: a kinship expressing the closest interaction of divine powers. The myth reveals how that bond acts through mutual support, amplification or the balancing of opposing forces.
rootOtherContext: The main names have different roots. Their powers can share a root in another context, revealed by the Greek word below.

pair.hera.zeus.myth: In the Theogony, Zeus and Hera form a royal marriage; Hebe, Ares and Eileithyia are named as their children. Authority and union sustain the divine family. In the Aurora Order’s interpretation, the monad of their combined total reveals the unity of two independent powers.
pair.hera.zeus.word.note: An oath binds intention to a promise for which one is answerable.
pair.poseidon.zeus.myth: In Iliad XX–XXI the conflict at Troy draws in the gods. Poseidon supports the Achaeans and challenges Apollo to a duel. Zeus allows the gods to enter battle and watches the clash. Zeus gives the other gods freedom to act while retaining supreme authority.
pair.poseidon.zeus.word.note: Saving power preserves life and the integrity of the shared world.
pair.demeter.zeus.myth: In the hymn to Demeter Zeus allows Persephone’s marriage to Hades. Demeter withholds the grain, and Zeus arranges the daughter’s return. The power of nourishment changes the decision of supreme authority.
pair.demeter.zeus.word.note: Sowing joins present work to a future harvest.
pair.athena.zeus.myth: In the Theogony, Athena is born from Zeus’s head. The myth joins supreme authority to intelligence and martial wisdom. In the Aurora Order’s interpretation, counsel and considered decisions express their combined action: power gains a clear design.
pair.athena.zeus.word.note: A considered decision joins intention to responsibility.
pair.apollo.zeus.myth: In Iliad XX–XXI the conflict at Troy draws in the gods. Apollo protects the Trojans and declines to fight Poseidon. Zeus allows the gods to enter battle and watches the clash. Zeus gives the other gods freedom to act while retaining supreme authority.
pair.apollo.zeus.word.note: Olympus gathers divine powers into a shared world.
pair.artemis.zeus.myth: In Iliad XX–XXI the conflict at Troy draws in the gods. Artemis stands with the Trojans and clashes with Hera. Zeus allows the gods to enter battle and watches the clash. Zeus gives the other gods freedom to act while retaining supreme authority.
pair.artemis.zeus.word.note: Olympus gathers divine powers into a shared world.

pair.ares.zeus.word.note: Themis embodies the order that sustains a shared world.

pair.hephaestus.zeus.word.note: Aether symbolises the height and brightness of the heavens.

pair.hermes.zeus.word.note: Aether symbolises the height and brightness of the heavens.

pair.hestia.zeus.word.note: A flame expresses the living power of fire that needs tending.
pair.dionysus.zeus.myth: In the Theogony Dionysus is born of Zeus and Semele, and Ariadne receives immortality through Zeus. Supreme order supports transformation and welcomes it into the immortal circle.
pair.dionysus.zeus.word.note: The maenad embodies feeling that moves beyond customary behaviour.
pair.hera.poseidon.myth: In Iliad XX–XXI the conflict at Troy draws in the gods. Hera supports the Achaeans and confronts Artemis. Poseidon supports the Achaeans and challenges Apollo to a duel. Here the gods support the same side and strengthen a shared undertaking.
pair.hera.poseidon.word.note: Courage helps us endure a clash and keep our direction.
pair.demeter.hera.myth: In the hymn to Demeter, the goddess stops grain from growing. People lose food, and the Olympian gods lose offerings. The return of fertility becomes a shared concern of the divine world. In the Aurora Order’s interpretation, this scene shows how every power needs nourishing support in order to act.
pair.demeter.hera.word.note: Persephone represents the connection between the depths of the earth and the return of spring.

pair.athena.hera.word.note: Victory expresses effort brought to fulfilment.

theme.conflict.life: A clash of powers can appear as an argument, competition or a struggle over who decides. Identify each side’s purpose and the cost of the clash.
theme.conflict.practice: Pause and name the actual issue. Separate the goal from the means of reaching it. Choose a rule that both sides can follow.
theme.authority.life: A decision needs a shared order, while each side has its own responsibility. Tension arises when authority and obligations drift apart.
theme.authority.practice: Clarify who decides, what they answer for and where the other person’s independence begins. Establish one clear shared rule.
theme.union.life: The connection appears in promises, shared roles and the expectation of support. A union grows stronger when each side understands the other’s contribution.
theme.union.practice: Make the mutual promise specific: who does what, and when. Leave room for each person to choose independently.
theme.care.life: A person wants results, while growth needs nourishment, time and attention. Exhaustion or anxiety can reveal which part of life needs care.
theme.care.practice: Identify what needs support: your energy, a relationship or a project. Choose one manageable act of care and allow it time to bear fruit.
theme.home.life: Movement and change need steady support: a place of return, a familiar rhythm or a dependable bond. Without that support, energy scatters.
theme.home.practice: Restore one support in your day: prepare a space, finish a simple task or agree on a time to return. Then move towards your goal again.
theme.change.life: Living change meets an established form. It can appear as inspiration, a strong feeling or the wish to leave a constricting routine.
theme.change.practice: Let the new experience find expression in a small action. Then preserve what matters in words, a plan or a finished piece of work.
theme.craft.life: An idea meets material and constraints. Tension becomes a result when the idea is tested through action and the work can be revised.
theme.craft.practice: Make a small prototype and test one property. Correct what obstructs the work before increasing its scale.
theme.speech.life: Two sides understand the same event differently. Mediation puts an intention into words that the other person can hear.
theme.speech.practice: State the main point in one sentence, then listen to the other person’s understanding. Find shared meaning before discussing terms and actions.
theme.clarity.life: Clear order meets living movement. A person needs to keep a direction while remaining responsive to changing circumstances.
theme.clarity.practice: Keep one clear point of reference and one flexible way to reach it. Check whether the rhythm helps, and adjust it if needed.
theme.boundaries.life: Closeness or shared work meets the need for personal space. A boundary allows powers to interact while retaining their independence.
theme.boundaries.practice: Name the terms of agreement and the limit. Discuss a way of meeting that leaves room for connection and independence.
theme.affection.life: Attraction gives an encounter energy, while subsequent action shapes the quality of the bond. Hear both desire and the other person’s response.
theme.affection.practice: Clarify the mutual desire and choose a small action that expresses it with care and clarity for both people.
otherRootContextText: The two words below express different aspects of the deities and reach the same root. In the Aurora Order’s interpretation, they reveal a kinship of powers within this context.
theme.alliance.life: Two powers support a shared goal. In life this is cooperation between different temperaments: one brings drive, another stability, clarity or skill. Their combined strength becomes fruitful when their actions are coordinated.
theme.alliance.practice: Name the shared goal and each person’s contribution. Agree on how to recognise the result and when to stop an unnecessary effort.
